name: Act of June 22, 1874 for the purchase of twenty sections from the Omaha for the Wisconsin Winnebago (18 Stat. 170)
promises: Not a treaty. The Act provided for buying twenty sections from the Omaha, along the boundary with the Winnebago reservation, on which to settle the Wisconsin Winnebago.
Royce records the purchase was completed by deed dated July 31, 1874 and covered 12,347.55 acres.
landTaken: 12,347.55 acres, bought by deed of July 31, 1874 (Royce).
today: No court or claims finding about this purchase was located.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 876-877

openQuestions: The price paid was not found in a source opened.
The Omaha dockets before the Indian Claims Commission (225-A, 225-C) concern the 1854 cession and trespass claims; none located concerns this sale.
The Omaha Tribe's own account of the sale was not searched in this pass.
